title: De transformatione serierum in fractiones continuas, ubi simul haec theoria non mediocriter amplificatur

deep.reconstruction:
Problem: turn an arbitrary alternating series s = 1/α − 1/β + 1/γ − 1/δ + … into a continued fraction. Euler first writes s = 1/(b + 1/(c + 1/(d + …))). From the previous pages (§§10–12) he has the partial denominators b = α, c = (β−α)/α², d = α²(γ−β)/β², e = β²(δ−γ)/(α²γ²), and so on.

Top of p.146: these are cleared of fractions: b = α, α²c = β−α, β²d = α²(γ−β), α²γ²e = β²(δ−γ), β²δ²f = α²γ²(ε−δ), etc.

§14: an equivalence transformation. Multiply the 2nd, 3rd, 4th, 5th, … partial fractions above and below by α², β², α²γ², β²δ², …. This gives s = 1/(b + α²/(α²c + α²β²/(β²d + α²β²γ²/(α²γ²e + …)))). Here the new denominators are exactly the cleared quantities above.

§15: substituting gives s = 1/(α + α²/(β−α + α²β²/(α²(γ−β) + α²β²γ²/(β²(δ−γ) + …)))). A second equivalence transformation divides the 3rd, 4th, 5th, … fractions by α², β², γ², …. This yields s = 1/(α + α²/(β−α + β²/(γ−β + γ²/(δ−γ + …)))).

Theorem I (§16): 1/s = α + α²/(β−α + β²/(γ−β + γ²/(δ−γ + …))).

§17: Euler remarks that the derivation went by detours ('per plures ambages'). He promises the direct method, which the next page supplies via the tails t, u, …. The page serves the paper's programme: obtain Brouncker's fraction for 4/π and the fraction for 1/ln 2 as special cases, then fractions for ∫x^{m−1}/(1+x^n) dx.
errors: None: the clearing of denominators and both equivalence transformations check out (e.g. α²β²/(α²(γ−β)+α²β²γ²/…) reduces to β²/(γ−β+β²γ²/…), and then dividing by β² gives γ²/(δ−γ+…)).
Convergence is not discussed. The identity holds formally, convergent by convergent: the n-th approximant equals the n-th partial sum. Euler, as usual, leaves the convergence question implicit.

ideas.what: Transforming an alternating series of reciprocals into a continued fraction whose approximants equal its partial sums: 1/s = α + α²/(β−α + β²/(γ−β + …))
ideas.modern_name: Euler's continued fraction formula (series ↔ continued fraction correspondence)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Euler (Introductio in analysin infinitorum, 1748, ch. 18; this paper E593)
ideas.where_published: Introductio, vol. I, ch. 18 (E101); E593 itself (Opuscula analytica II, 1785)

ideas.what: Equivalence transformations: multiplying successive partial numerators and denominators by chosen factors to clear fractions, then dividing out common factors
ideas.usually_credited_to: Standard technique; Euler used it throughout
ideas.where_published: E101 ch. 18; various continued-fraction papers by Euler

deep.surprise_reason: The page derives the classical Euler continued-fraction formula, which is well known and credited to Euler (already in the Introductio). The algebra is correct and contains no new idea.
transcription_corrections: §14 opening is partly illegible in the scan: 'Nunc ipsam fractionem [continuam ita repraesentemus, vt in ea] eaedem formulae occurrant' — the bracketed words are a conjectural reading.
Top of page reads 'b = α' and 'ααc = β − α', consistent with the transcription.
